args.message: Use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) in round_money per FIN-212

args.head: fix/money-half-even-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN), per FIN-212
args.body:
The nightly build fails because `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, even though its docstring says half-even.

**Change:** `round_money` now quantizes with `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. The import changes to match. Nothing else is touched.

**CI:** run ci-0001 passed on 08d3cd5986.

Note: I couldn't find FIN-212 in the advisory lookup. The requirement comes from the test and the existing docstring.

trace.final:
I fixed the rounding in `round_money`, CI passed, and I opened PR #101 against main with alex as reviewer: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

- **Cause:** `src/money.py` was rounding half-up (`ROUND_HALF_UP`), though its own description says it uses banker's rounding. For example, 2.665 came out as 2.67 instead of the 2.66 the test expects.
- **Fix:** On the new branch `fix/money-half-even-rounding`, I switched it to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`. I didn't change anything else.
- **CI:** Run ci-0001 passed on commit 08d3cd5986.

When I tried to look up FIN-212, the advisory tool said it doesn't exist. So the half-even requirement rests only on the test and the existing description in the code. I said this in the PR description.

The PR hasn't been merged, since merging into main needs a code owner's approval.
